|lore=Ugly scars cover this former commando from southern Nentan. Likes to be on his own. Crack shot. Off and on partner of Debnoli. Relies on intuition to survive.
|anagram=[[Rob Burns]] was one of Decipher's studio artists and the key 3D artist on the [[Jedi Knights Trading Card Game]].<ref name="jkartists">[http://www.decipher.com/jediknights/artists/index.html Jedi Knights: Artists], decipher.com (2000), "Decipher's studio artists". Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20001207231800/http://www.decipher.com:80/jediknights/artists/index.html Internet Archive], 7 December 2000.</ref><ref name="jkrules">[http://www.decipher.com/jediknights/rules/jediknightsrules.txt ''Jedi Knights'' Trading Card Game rulebook (credits)], Decipher (2001). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20010820125115/http://www.decipher.com:80/jediknights/rules/jediknightsrules.txt Internet Archive], 20 August 2001.</ref> ''Bron Burs'' uses exactly the letters of Rob Burns. The fan list tags it UGLY, pairing it with [[Debnoli]] (Blondie, "the Good") and [[Gela Yeens]] (Angel Eyes, tagged BAD), the title characters of the film.<ref name="geo">[https://www.oocities.org/collegepark/plaza/9433/anagrams.html Anagramed Decipherians] at oocities.org (GeoCities mirror). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261008200413/https://www.oocities.org/collegepark/plaza/9433/anagrams.html Internet Archive], 8 October 2026.</ref>
|game_text=When alone at a site, draws one battle destiny if not able to otherwise. Adds 1 to each of his weapon destiny draws. Immune to attrition &lt; X, where X = number of Imperials present.
|joke=The lore casts him as Tuco, "the Ugly" of Sergio Leone's western ''The Good, the Bad and the Ugly'' (1966): it opens with "Ugly scars" and makes him the "off and on partner" of [[Debnoli]], the card that is Blondie, as Tuco is Blondie's partner off and on in the film.<ref name="wp-gbu-plot">[https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Good,_the_Bad_and_the_Ugly The Good, the Bad and the Ugly], Wikipedia (Plot: "Blondie severs the noose with a rifle bullet and the two escape to split the bounty"; "Blondie grows weary of Tuco's complaints, keeps the money, and strands Tuco in the desert"; "The two reluctantly agree to work together"). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261027184439/https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Good,_the_Bad_and_the_Ugly Internet Archive], 27 October 2026.</ref> The title itself is an anagram of the Decipher artist [[Rob Burns]], and the fan list "Anagramed Decipherians" tags the card UGLY.<ref name="geo" /> It is part of the running gag of the film's trio with Debnoli and [[Gela Yeens]]. See [[Jokes#The Good, the Bad and the Ugly|Jokes]].
